archive.interpretation: The base commit is ancestry, not a claim that all release bytes equal that Git tree. The archive SHA and per-member SHA bind this audit.

boundary_definitions.phase_preflight: Before first llama_decode of this phase; no new native computation by this phase.
boundary_definitions.operator_preflight: Inside llama_decode but before this operator launches; earlier native operations/groups may already have modified owner.
boundary_definitions.post_native: After native launch/decode/synchronization; owner must not be silently reused on failure.
boundary_definitions.assertion: GGML_ASSERT/abort is process termination, not a caught recoverable unsupported state.

exclusions.reason: No independent project-specific recipe implementation audited here. Files named native_q4 in prior work denote four query columns and are not evidence for Q4_K weights.
Generic upstream Vulkan files in CUDA sourcekit do not bind the paper-specific Vulkan implementation. No Vulkan guard row inferred from prose.

findings.statement: Packed Q8 is not covered by backend-loop4 marker guards; generic dispatch and graph fallback are present.
Placement observer is capture-only and its original filter excludes packed projection names; M2 broadens the filter.
Target-group failures explicitly poison; trim/draft/sample failures are contained by CLI process exit.
Actual policy/prefix/head-placement keys exist; frontend structural Identity helper is not the live key.

guards.title: Dense cache ownership and append preflight
predicate: Nonempty call; not poisoned; memory dynamically casts to llama_kv_cache; n_stream==1; no SWA; no shifted cells; width>0.
used==occupied_end==physical_head==position; position+width<=capacity using uint64_t; each cell before position is occupied at its own position and contains sequence 0.
Returned extent count equals input count; K and V are F16. Per-row padding uses max(n_pad,256), clipped by actual capacity.
guards.failure_before_execution: Before the first llama_decode of this phase: unsupported/malformed cache returns an empty extent vector; need throws. No new native decode has occurred and PhaseContext is not poisoned by these preflight failures.
guards.failure_after_execution: The later post-call mapping check is separate (G07). This preflight does not make a partially executed call recoverable.
guards.fallback_behavior: No automatic R replay/fallback in this executor; caller gets failure.
guards.supported_scope: Dense nonwrapping sequence-0 append; frontend uses one sequence per batch and a fixed resident owner. seq_has(0) is not an exclusivity test for arbitrary externally mutated multi-sequence caches.

observed_evidence.detail: Release frontend and reconstructed M2 share this gate. The helper checks physical metadata, not token equality or KV byte equality.

missing_qualification: Fault-inject gap/shift/head/capacity violations on the bound native implementation and assert zero new decode calls plus unchanged owner before rejection.
For a reusable API accepting externally modified caches, explicitly bind single-sequence ownership or reject cells with additional sequence owners.

guards.title: Whole versus local plan, width and output reserve

anchors: M2 explicit k3/7 reserve8 D4 contract

predicate: SIMPLE groups adjacent equal extents and equal arithmetic_class, maximum 32 rows; LOCAL takes chunks of at most 32 and delegates physical cuts to attention.
Frontend arithmetic_class is only 1+type_k+(type_v<<8). It is not a complete projection/backend/placement recipe identifier.
Original release all-output reserve gate is 4 rows. Reconstructed M2 uses phase_target_reserve; its entry binds reserve 8. Last-only output requests can span wider phases.
guards.failure_before_execution: Invalid SIMPLE positions/extents, unknown lowering, or all-output count above the reserve throw before native execution. LOCAL relies on G01 for position/extent support.
guards.failure_after_execution: After execution starts, later failures use G07/G08; a new lower-width plan is not silently retried.
guards.fallback_behavior: No automatic scalar replay. Unsupported projection scope has separate behavior (G03/G04).
guards.supported_scope: Fixed frontend profile; request masks exposed by this interface are all rows or last row, not arbitrary sparse masks.

observed_evidence.detail: The live plan stores original output flags but its arithmetic class alone cannot justify the method section’s general typed recipe. The original k3 all-output cap does not certify M2 k7.

missing_qualification: Bind the recipe fingerprint to frozen deployment metadata outside this two-type arithmetic_class, or narrow the paper wording to this implementation.
Qualify reserve-8 M2 separately; retain original reserve-4 experiments as their own scope.

guards.title: Packed Q8 projection admission and unmarked dispatch
predicate: Outer path: hs_query_batch; Q8_0 weight; F32 activation; 5<=q<=32; activation ne[2]==ne[3]==1.

Packing additionally requires contiguous activation, weight ne[2]==ne[3]==1, q>=8. It maps complete groups to [K,4,floor(q/4)], reshapes outputs, and sends remaining columns through ordinary <=4-column matmuls.
Packed nodes have no hs_loop4 marker. Actual kernel selection remains the ordinary CUDA dispatcher: bad padding can choose cuBLAS; otherwise MMVF/MMF/MMVQ/MMQ/cuBLAS selection runs.

The packed branch does not itself check actual same-device CUDA buffers, NVIDIA warp32, old-tile MMVQ selection, weight contiguity, or the loop4 integer-offset bounds. These cannot be borrowed from the marked-control path.
guards.failure_before_execution: Failed graph packing predicate selects <=4-column graph operations; failure of the outer predicate selects the ordinary wide matmul. Neither branch reports a typed recipe-unsupported status.
guards.failure_after_execution: Ordinary backend assertions/errors can fail during llama_decode; caught exceptions poison PhaseContext, assertions may terminate the process. The missing marked predicate is not itself a detected failure.
guards.fallback_behavior: Shape/layout fallback and generic backend dispatch are present. They are not established here as a qualified reference-compatible fallback for every descriptor outside the measured profile.
guards.supported_scope: Static path identification for the published CUDA Q8 packed core. No observed numerical error or fallback trigger is claimed for the frozen measured configuration.

observed_evidence.detail: Packed and loop4 graph members are independently pinned. Their CUDA dispatcher/MMVQ files are byte-identical, but only loop4 build_lora_mm marks the node. Four-column MMVQ has an explicit case-4 specialization; grouped channels affect launch dimensions and offsets.

missing_qualification: Replay captured operands with packed-versus-loop4 descriptors and record actual kernel/reduction identity, stride arithmetic, buffer device and padding branch.
Add explicit packed recipe admission before any native work, or a marked per-operator validator with fail-closed owner invalidation. No numerical-core change is proposed as qualified by this audit.

Adversarial descriptor cases must include bad-padding compute views, noncontiguous activation/weights, foreign placement and q/tail boundaries; expected outcomes must distinguish reject from separately qualified fallback.

guards.title: Backend-loop4 explicit shape, placement and dispatch guard

anchors: old tile dispatch is not MMVQ

predicate: Marked MUL_MAT; Q8_0/F32/F32; all three tensors contiguous with singleton ne[2:4]; q in 5..32; K/M/q dimensions agree; bounded positive dimensions; no precision hint.
Guarded integer row-block and quantized/output offset spans; no IDs or fused arithmetic.
NVIDIA CUDA only, actual buffers on ctx.device, warp_size==32, no unsafe padded compute view; each original 1..4-column tile must select MMVQ rather than MMVF/MMF.
guards.failure_before_execution: These are before this marked operator’s quantizer/kernel, but occur inside llama_decode: earlier operators or groups may already have changed state. Do not call them whole-phase preflight.
guards.failure_after_execution: Thrown exceptions propagate to PhaseContext catch, which poisons the owner. No success record is emitted; process-level catch returns failure.
guards.fallback_behavior: Marked failures throw; they do not silently fall through to ordinary matmul. A graph node never marked is outside this guarantee.
guards.supported_scope: Strong backend-loop4 control only. The marker and guard do not apply to packed nodes or arbitrary Q4/Vulkan paths.

observed_evidence.detail: Control quantizes the wide activation once and loops over exactly old 4-column/tail specializations with checked offsets. This is a source-backed guard distinction, not a performance or equivalence measurement.

missing_qualification: Native own-path and cross-path replay must validate that quantizing all columns together preserves the admitted activations.
Fault injection must show post-entry failures invalidate owner even when earlier graph work completed.

guards.title: Local attention physical views and arithmetic descriptor
predicate: Grouped path requires active hs_query_batch, causal/non-Flash, consecutive positions and one unique sequence, matching prefix count, more than one row, one K/V stream, no bias/sinks/MLA.
Local grouping arithmetic is Q/K/V dtype; dispatch encodes Q head dimension, Q/K head counts and V transposition, with <=65535 asserted field bounds.

Groups share extent and descriptor; layout 0 uses tiles<=4. K, V and mask views use that extent; mask is made contiguous when needed. Query-batch attention restricts architecture to LLAMA/QWEN3 and dense nonexpert non-Flash shapes.
guards.failure_before_execution: Graph construction uses ordinary branch if grouped predicate is false. Specific attention constraints are GGML_ASSERT: they abort rather than returning a recoverable unsupported result.
guards.failure_after_execution: Graph construction follows native batch/cache planning; do not promise unchanged owner on an assertion. Process termination precludes reuse, but catch(...)/poisoned does not catch abort.
guards.fallback_behavior: The ordinary attention branch exists. Outside the bound dense profile its numerical equivalence is not established merely by falling through.
guards.supported_scope: Fixed non-Flash dense LLAMA/QWEN3 attention recipe with singleton stream; no claim for paged/wrapping/SWA/MoE/MLA or arbitrary layouts.

observed_evidence.detail: Physical views and mask materialization are explicit. The graph also depends on guards that are assertions, not typed admission statuses.

missing_qualification: Add native descriptor rejection tests and original-reference state/vector comparisons around padding boundaries.
Either describe assertion termination accurately or move unsupported-layout checks to preflight for a recoverable serving API.

guards.title: Actual graph-reuse predicates
predicate: Reuse compares policy={backend=cuda,layout,prefix=active,f32_q8_activation=false,scalar_head_norm_offload=active,implementation=1} and the full prefix extent vector.

Existing graph parameters compare hs_query_batch, ubatch topology/sequence metadata, n_outputs and other model graph settings. Rotary head-scale placement key compares relevant tensor types/shapes, host placement and backend offload decisions.
Requested-output row indices are refreshed by set_input; arbitrary request-mask identity need not be in topology key if output count matches.
refplan::Identity(deployment,phase,lowering,rows) is declared in phase_plan.hpp but is not referenced by the audited frontend; live reuse relies on the above core predicates.
guards.failure_before_execution: Mismatch returns false and rebuilds the graph; it does not fail the request or restore a prior state.
guards.failure_after_execution: A subsequent execution failure uses the owner failure path; reuse rejection is not a native failure.
guards.fallback_behavior: Rebuild is an expected topology adaptation, not reference replay.
guards.supported_scope: Frozen model/backend/context deployment. There is no generic runtime projection recipe object compared by this key, nor a literal phase-label comparison.

observed_evidence.detail: The actual reuse protection is stronger than a bare shape key, but the unused frontend Identity helper must not be cited as the implementation of the paper claim.

missing_qualification: Qualify transitions changing prefix vector while outer shape stays fixed, layout/active policy, head placement and requested rows.
Describe fixed model/module binding separately from dynamic reuse identity; add a packed recipe fingerprint if recipe selection becomes mutable.

guards.title: Requested output ownership and append postcondition
predicate: Each group uses original requested flags (all or last); synchronization precedes copying each requested full vocabulary vector into PhaseContext-owned storage.
Requested logits pointer must exist; used_max_p1 must equal the expected append end. logits(row) rejects absent/unrequested rows. sample checks all entries finite and retains lowest index on ties.
OutputRows helper is not used here; the live owner is vector<vector<float>>. Postcondition checks extent/end, not reference KV bytes.
guards.failure_before_execution: Output reserve gate precedes execution (G02). A consumer requesting an unrequested output is rejected; it is not produced retroactively.
guards.failure_after_execution: Missing requested pointer, post-append mapping mismatch, or observed placement failure inside decode poisons the owner. A sample nonfinite failure is outside the PhaseContext catch and terminates via entry catch.
guards.fallback_behavior: No hidden extra output-mask/reserve expansion and no retry after native failure.
guards.supported_scope: Original reserve-4 frontend; M2 reserve changes must be qualified separately. Owned vectors survive later group scratch reuse.

observed_evidence.detail: The implementation matches the ownership order needed by the induction argument, but not a run-time equality check against R.

missing_qualification: Native multi-group tests selecting an earlier accepted frontier must compare full logits and active KV against the independent reference.
Corrupt/missing output and postcondition failure injections should verify that no success result or reused owner escapes.

guards.title: Commit, pending token, reset and failure ownership boundary
predicate: Corrections/bonuses remain pending until the next decode; native commit logic stops at cap/EOG, and keep=base+1+accepted trims both owners.
Target native group execution and postchecks are enclosed in a catch-all that sets poisoned=true; subsequent plan.clear/decode reject that owner.
Context::trim, reset postcheck, draft decode and sample are outside that poison catch. The published entry catches exceptions and exits failure, preventing another request in that process.
guards.failure_before_execution: An already-poisoned owner rejects clear/decode before reset or new execution.
guards.failure_after_execution: Target decode exceptions poison. Trim/draft/sample failures rely on process exit rather than setting target.plan.poisoned. GGML assertions/abort terminate directly.
guards.fallback_behavior: No automatic replay into the same partially updated owner.
guards.supported_scope: CLI worker termination contract; not yet a general reusable service object whose callers may catch trim/sample/draft errors and continue.

observed_evidence.detail: The statement failed native call invalidates owner is implemented at two different boundaries. The target-group poison rule is explicit; other transaction failures are contained by process lifetime.

missing_qualification: For embedding into a persistent library API, add a transaction-level owner-invalid flag covering trim, draft, reset and sampling before allowing caller recovery.
Retain independent-reference tests for cap/EOG/correction/bonus and prior accepted frontier; this static audit creates none.

guards.title: Placement observation is capture-specific and version-specific
predicate: Clean target phases set phase_observe=false; callback returns immediately, leaving bad at its reset default unless some other code changes it.
Original release heavy observer only selects kq*/hs_* names and requires device description containing 5070. frontier_packed_* projection names do not match that name filter.
Reconstructed Linux M2 additionally selects MUL_MAT and checks GPU device type instead of the 5070 substring.
Entry selects one GPU and requests all layers there, but those configuration requests are not an independent per-operator same-device dispatch guard.
guards.failure_before_execution: The single-GPU admission can reject initialization. There is no always-on clean placement observation from Observer::callback.
guards.failure_after_execution: Heavy observer bad status is checked after native execution and poisons target PhaseContext. Clean need(!obs.bad) by itself cannot attest placement.
guards.fallback_behavior: No evidence here that measured clean execution moved to CPU or another device. The finding is an observation/guard scope distinction, not an observed placement failure.
guards.supported_scope: Original RTX capture filter and reconstructed Linux capture filter must be reported separately; neither is a general clean recipe guard.

observed_evidence.detail: Static control flow proves the clean observer bypass. Marked loop4 still has G04 placement checks; packed does not acquire those checks merely by sharing backend source.

missing_qualification: Bind clean result to qualified loaded modules/model/device and capture recipe fingerprints for all admitted packed nodes.
If clean dynamic placement safety is claimed, add a cheap always-on per-operator validator and charge its cost; capture-only logs remain qualification evidence.

guards.title: Diagnostic full-vector/native-state capture is separate from clean guard
predicate: Capture requires binary32/little endian, a valid context/model/new output directory, requested frontier present/finite, and nonzero complete native sequence export.
The release snapshot call observes initial and first commit only. Reconstructed M2 expands snapshot coverage to all requested capture points.
Raw sequence.bin requires active KV extraction; exported bytes are not automatically the reference active-state relation.
guards.failure_before_execution: Capture/path/format failures throw; this diagnostic is not on the clean request path.
guards.failure_after_execution: Capture may run after state changes. Failures reach the process boundary, not the target decode poison catch.
guards.fallback_behavior: No capture is fabricated by changing output reservation or requested rows.
guards.supported_scope: Offline heavy qualification only; no native reference replay or state equality comparison was executed by this audit.

observed_evidence.detail: The capture source supports collecting evidence but does not itself compare R or certify all phases/shapes.

missing_qualification: Tie independent R and candidate captures to the exact deployment binary/source, compare full vectors and extracted active KV, and retain per-case coverage rather than extrapolating from helper presence.
